text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic received U.N. administrator for Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein. Their talks centred on measures to revitalise the area.
- Yugoslav-German economic talks start in Belgrade. Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic said normalisation of relations with the European Union was of extreme importance for Yugoslavia.
- Yugosalv and Macedonian Defence ministers agree to open military missions in Skopje and Belgrade shortly.
- We have determined basis to widely expand Yugoslav Russian cooperation already by the end of the year, says Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Nikola Sainovic in Moscow.
- Bor copper mines complex concludes deal with the Macedonian copper mine Bucim to process between 45 and 50 thousand tonnes of copper a year.

- Yugoslav living standards are at the 1992 level and can be expected to improve by two to three percent a month if current real growth of wages continues, coupled with relatively stable prices, says deputy director of federal statistics office Dragisa Bjeloglav.
- Exports expected to double in the last quarter in relation to the same period last year, says Serbian government foreign trade coordination team.
- Serbian government regulations on sales in open air markets entered into effect on Monday and Serbian chief market inspector Stojan Zdravkovic says illicit trade will no longer be tolerated.
- Begej shipyard in Zrenjanin hands over two vessels to a Norwegian buyer, the first after the lifting of the sanctions.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic cancels meeting with U.N. Human Rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn according to independent news agency Beta.

- Representatives of the IMF and the World Bank are expected to come to Belgrade within the next two months, a visit which would mark the beginning of "real" talks with them, says spokesman for Lowe Bell financial, Yugoslav public relations adviser.
- Yugoslav minister in charge of human rights Margit Savovic receives U.N. Human rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn to discuss recent Serbian-Kosovo Albanian education agreement.
- Belgrade-Zagreb railway link expected to be restored by end of year at the latest, says assistant director general of Yugoslav railways Radomir Jovanovic.
